correctness.rationale: In canonical zero-sum Euclidean H, the polar inequalities |y_u-y_v|<=1 yield integral extremal potentials by a spanning tree of active edges. Diameter two forces two-level or single-part three-level extremes; their squared norms are j(N-j)/N and t-(b-a)²/N, giving M=max(floor(N²/4)/N, L-(L mod 2)/N), with singleton L=1 harmless. Central symmetry centers an optimal ball. Farthest polar normals span H for binary balance; when three-level T>B their rank is h(L-1) for even L, and hL except one relation if maximal parts exhaust all vertices for odd L. Orthogonality to these antipodal normals and strictness of all others gives exact affine center-set dimension. Independent exact polar-potential brute force/rational rank checks for (1,1,1),(2,2,2),(2,2,2,2),(3,3,3),(4,2,2,1) matched the radius, contact counts and dimensions.
